I found no source on the character's current copyright status, and I did not check ownership or renewal records for it. The cartoon's own story may also be separate from the character. The story layer is therefore undetermined.

editorial:
The Underground World is the sixteenth of seventeen Technicolor Superman cartoons made for Paramount. It was released June 18, 1943, runs about eight minutes, and was directed by Seymour Kneitel and produced by Sam Buchwald. Jay Morton wrote the story and Sammy Timberg composed the music. Jackson Beck is credited as narrator and Julian Noa as Perry White. Other cast credits are not stated here because the sources I checked disagreed. The Internet Archive item description describes the plot as an homage to Burroughs's 'At the Earth's Core'.

The rights trap is Superman himself. Even if the print of the cartoon proves free, the character is a separate asset with its own rights, and I did not verify its current status. I also did not check any trademark registration for the name or logo. No renewal search was performed for this dossier. Check the Copyright Office public catalog and the Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1970 and 1971 yourself before treating the print as public domain.
faq: Is The Underground World (1943) free to use?

Not confirmed. No renewal search was performed. Check the Copyright Office records and the Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1970 and 1971 before relying on the print. The Superman character and name may carry separate rights, and I did not verify them.
Can I make new Superman content from this cartoon?

Not on the strength of this dossier. The cartoon's copyright and the Superman character's rights are separate questions, and I verified neither the character's status nor any trademark. Get independent legal advice before creating new Superman stories, merchandise, or branding.
